No lid, hinges or handles. KIT (fix): g1_loading_station.glb drops the uniform 1.54x y-stretch. It is now the uniform-scale mesh (as g1_loading_block) with a piecewise y-remap (models.json spreadY, 10 slabs) that keeps every rivet row at scale 1. That covers the judge's three bands (bottom strap 0-0.12 m, the mid seam +-0.06 m round its double row, the top frame and deck 0.20 m under the top) plus the 8 rows of the end-frame and centre-batten rivet columns, which a three-band remap would have stretched 1.84x. Only the plain plate between the rows stretches (2.35x, no visible banding in the texture) to reach 1.83 m. Result: 2.74 x 1.83 x 1.59 m, 13409 faces, atlas re-baked by import; the rivets are round (kit renders in g1_G). g1_loading_block.glb (2.74 x 1.19 x 1.59 m, undistorted) is unchanged. assets.notes: PASS 2 (p2b, 44 credits; the fix round spent 0). Concept: nano-banana-pro, 16:9, background removed, the judge's prompt word for word (task 01a13830, candidate c5); it meets the accept list. Image-to-3D with --geo 2k (35 credits, task 01a13832): a clean 35k-triangle mesh, posts every 0.444 units, 5 Warren panels across 4 bays. THE UNREAL KIT (groups/g3/p2b/kit, built by p2b/tools/catwalk_kit.py; metres, Y up, +Z the front; each piece a GLB with crease-angle normals and a 2k JPEG base colour, plus OBJ/MTL). Pieces: catwalk_bay (x 0..0.9143, tileable: half a post at each end) and, new in the fix round, catwalk_bay_b / _c / _d, the same bay cut from the source's other three bays. Each carries its own texture (the toe-plate scratches and rail wear differ). All four share the truss panel and the joint sections, so they tile in any order. Mixing them answers the repeating toe-plate scratches with real texture rather than a UV offset. catwalk_end_l / catwalk_end_r: the end posts, rail end caps, deck and truss ends. catwalk_run3: end_l + bay_b + bay_c + bay + end_r, the source's bays 0, 1 and 2 in their own order (2.743 m between the end posts, 3.0 m overall). catwalk_grating (new, optional): a masked grating plane for one bay at y 0.372 (1 mm over the Meshy grating's highest point, 0.3706), z -0.370..0.364. It has bearing bars every 30.5 mm across the walkway and 7 cross rods, a PNG alpha cut-out (alphaMode MASK 0.5, double-sided) and tiles with the bays. It hides the generated grating's lumps and holes. Chord fix: the source panel's chord is not level. Its underside rises 0.0015 units over the panel's last 0.11 while its top face stays put, so the 2 copies a bay stepped at every bottom node. The step was 2.2 mm (measured), not the 1 cm I claimed in round 1. Under its top face the chord is now stretched down to the level underside by the measured profile. Over a 5-bay run the underside now steps at most 0.11 mm (round 1: 2.25 mm). The front chord's top face keeps a 1.5 mm drift within each panel, which steps back under the diagonals' feet at the nodes. Measured (catwalk_kit.json): top rail 0.93 m over the deck; knee rail 0.43 m; 0.955 m over the posts; 0.74 m of grating; truss 0.32 m deep and constant; nothing below it. Tiling test kit/_tiling_test_5bays.obj: end_l + bay_b, bay, bay_d, bay_c, bay + end_r. At its 6 joints the sections either side differ by a median 0.15-2.9 mm (round 1: 2.4-3.0 mm). The textured front render shows posts, rails, toe plates and truss continuous (review sheet). THE SPRITE 'catwalk' is re-rendered from the fixed kit. Its source (p2b/tools/cw_sprite_src.py) is end_l + 3 x catwalk_bay + end_r, one bay three times. It drops the front handrail and the back truss, as before. (2) Each rail span between the fittings is smoothed to one tone a row: the knee rail's y26 is steel[5] along every span, with the fittings darker. assets.notes: PASS 2 (p2b, 42 credits; the fix round spent 0). Two nano-banana-2 concepts, 16:9, background removed. c2 is the judge's prompt word for word (guides only 1.7 m apart; not used); c3 has the guides near the ends and was used (2 buntons, not 3). Standard image-to-3D (30 credits, task 01a13833): a clean 38k-triangle back wall. THE UNREAL KIT (groups/g4/p2b/kit, built by p2b/collar_kit.py; metres, Y up, the brick face at z 0, x 0 the shaft's centre line, a uniform 2.694 m per unit; inner span 4.57 m = the level's 5-tile E shaft, 2.79 m tall). Pieces: shaft_collar_full (as generated, guides 3.16 m apart), shaft_collar_wall (guides off, patched), shaft_collar_guide (one 0.15 m timber guide), shaft_collar_level_e (the wall + guides at x +-1.829, 3.657 m apart, as tiles.js shaftPx paints them). Judge's fixes: (1) The sagging lower bunton is replaced in full, wall and level_e by a copy of the upper I-beam. It moves down 0.944 m (0.3505 units), the measured flange-to-flange offset: the I-beams are at y 0.666-0.822 and 1.606-1.768 m. The judge's 0.957 m came from my round-1 band constants, which were 4-6 mm off the real flanges. The copy spans the returns' inner faces in front of the brick (z > 0.013 m). In full it leaves the guides' widths alone, because the guides stand in front there. The bright wedge is gone in the judge's lvl_e_34 view. (2) The patches at the old guide spots are cut per member: brick below and above the upper bunton, the upper bunton, and the slab face (the lower bunton is the upper one's copy). The bunton and slab strips are searched along the member, clear of both guides, on the bunton's true I-beam stretches. The search wants matching end tones, an even inside (no chart seams), a flat face and no stains. Each patch's texels are toned by a factor that runs linearly from its left neighbour's tone to its right neighbour's. The toned texels live in a copy of the atlas, so collar_texture.png is now 2048x4096: the bottom half is the Meshy atlas, the top half the toned copy for the patch triangles. Measured on a front albedo raster at 250 px/m, the largest mean-colour difference across a patch edge (4 cm either side, RGB 0-255) fell from 12.4 to 3.9. The slab fell from 10.5-12.4 to at most 2.4, the buntons from 4.3-7.5 to at most 3.9, and the brick is at most 2.1. (3) The returns' red-brown brick is tinted in the texture to the back wall's soot-black-grey. It is a Lab mean/spread transfer (L*a*b* 26.4/1.4/3.2 -> 20.0/0.5/1.5) on the 1.61M texels the returns' visible faces use, with 3 px padding and never a texel the back wall uses (UV overlap 0). The untinted atlas is kept as collar_texture_meshy.png, and collar_kit.json notes it. (4) LODs: collar_kit.json gives the import settings: UE5 Nanite on (about 40k triangles), otherwise Unreal's own LOD reduction (3 LODs, or the LevelArchitecture LOD group). No offline LOD files ship. Meshy's UV charts are fragmented (73k UV corners on 26k positions), and a seam-keeping simplifier (meshoptimizer simplifyWithAttributes, tried at 30% and 10%) stalls at about 85% of the triangles. The cuts now split only the triangles they touch: full 39.2k, wall 41.1k, level_e 43.2k, guide 1.1k triangles. Known nit: in the flat-shaded kit previews the bunton webs show faint diagonal facet lines from Meshy's slightly twisted web faces. The copy now carries them on both buntons. The GLBs' crease normals soften them. THE SPRITE 'g4_shaft_collar' (OPTIONAL, unshipped: the level keeps tiles.js shaftPx; SHIP_COLLAR False) is re-imported from the new level_e. It is 236x147 px, anchor 118,146, yaw 0, pitch 10, open ends. (a) The guides' feet under the floor line are trimmed and the last row (146) is coal[0], so the sprite is 236x147 with ay 146. (b) No lit relief specks: each sink zone's brick is capped at its face step, which removes the brick[2] dashes on rows 80, 100 and 125. (c) Under the 93 px step the joints are coal[0], as shaftPx darkens its mortar, so the courses stay legible down to 126 px. (d) The floor past 126 px is coal[0] (pitBack's last fade). (e) The slab's lit top is 3 rows (stone[3]) all along. Also, the guide tops (row 5) are timber instead of 4 px of brick and concrete specks. Checks: 0 off-ramp pixels; 20 isolated pixels (round 1: 54). Tooling added to groups/g4/ms.mjs: box 'max', courses 'to' / 'col', 'trim' (as G3's) and 'px' (final-sprite pixel rects). The other 8 g4 sprites (sheave frames included) are pixel-identical to pass 1 and to round 1. Backups: groups/g4/backup_p1 (pass 1), groups/g4/p2b/kit_r1 and groups/g4/p2b/fix (round 1).

judge_history.reroll: Kit only: the 3D model is a 4:1 T3D stack stretched 4.66x in y, so the brick courses are about 1.3 m tall and the iron bands are 4.66x too thick. Not usable in Unreal. Preferred, 0 credits: lathe the profile in Python (octagonal base 2.3 m x 3 m, a round shaft tapering 1.5 to 0.9 m over 30 m, bands every 4 m, a corbelled cap). Use cylindrical UVs with a tileable crop of the current T3D brick texture, repeated so one course is about 7.5 cm. Meshy option for pass 2 (about 60 credits): a 3-piece modular kit, each piece close to cubic proportions, which T3D handles well. 'octagonal red-brick chimney base 2.4 m across, 3 m tall, stone plinth and cornice, no ground, no text'; 'straight round red-brick chimney shaft section 1.5 m diameter, 4 m tall, slight taper, one iron band, flat seamless top and bottom, no ground, no text'; 'corbelled brick chimney crown 1.6 m wide, 1.5 m tall, soot-blackened top, two iron warning-lamp brackets, no ground, no text'. Rendered with the pass-1 renderer unchanged (groups/g8/char/char_page.js + render_char.mjs; new config groups/g8/char/cfg_p2e.py -> chars_p2e.json, the pass-1 class tables and ramps; both facings, yaw 0.35 / pi - 0.35, pitch 4, 52.5 px/m, 1 px outline #0b080b, sockets per frame), then appended under the pass-1 atlas by groups/g8/p2e/tools/merge_atlas.py (new clips carry pack: 2; pass-1 clips untouched; pass-1 copies in groups/g8/p2e/backup_pass1/). No frame touches the render window's edge (p2e/tools/clipcheck.py). Every action id was verified with 'mk.py library --search' and previewed from Meshy's public preview GIFs (groups/g8/p2e/gif*/sheet_*.png) before buying; none duplicates the character's pack 1. Unreal: the FBX next to the GLB in the anim dir, on the pass-1 rig. FIX of a pass-1 defect: knock_down frames 6-17 were cut by the 150 x 130 px render window (the flip went past its top, the lying body past its side); re-rendered from the pass-1 action GLB in a 230 x 160 window and swapped into the atlas (clip marked fix: 'p2e', old pixels cleared). Atlas now 23 clips, 2091 x 4661 px (taller than 4096: fine for canvas 2D; split into two pages if a WebGL target caps textures at 4096). Sheets: groups/g8/review/g8_regime_officer_anims2_right_x2.png / _left_x2.png (pack 2 only); the full groups/g8/review/g8_regime_officer_anims_right_x2.png / _left_x2.png regenerated. || P2E FIX ROUND (judge p2e round 1; no Meshy spend). (1) gunshot_reaction is EXCLUDED, both rows; the JSON 'excluded' gives the reason. It was the strongest salute read of the job, and the +-1.2 rad salvage fails as it does for the guard (review/g8_p2e_gunshot_salvage_test_x2.png). (2) Pistol. Round 1's note 'the pistol is composited at hand_r' was not true: no pistol existed. It is now hand-pixeled in out/models.png / .json as 'pistol' / 'pistol_l', 9 x 5 px: a dark blued slide on steel[2] with a lit top line of steel[5] so it reads against his grey gloves, a steel[1] grip and the #0b080b outline. draw_pistol / holster_pistol carry prop = {pistol: hand_r, rifle: none}, and each frame has frames[i].prop = {sprite, x, y, layer: over}. The muzzle sits 3 px past the fingertips, because the gloved hands are ~11 px long and hide a pistol held at the palm. A frame without prop means the pistol is holstered: draw frames 0-1 right / 0 left, holster from frame 4 right / 7 left. Demo: review/g8_p2e_props_x3.png. (3) crouch_and_step_back keeps all 27 frames; a motion edit replaces the cut. The right arm (RightShoulder to RightHand, 0.5-1.75 s) is slerped to its hanging start pose, so frames 12-14 no longer throw it straight forward with an open hand. The left hand still flinches to his face, and in the left profile both arms swing out for balance. (4) shouting_angrily is re-rendered as two segments, 0-0.5 s + 1.5-2.15 s (9 frames): he leans in and bellows. The 0.5-1.5 s hop and back-turn are cut as asked. So is the rest of the clip, because 2.2-4.5 s holds a second hop with fists overhead and an arms-spread tantrum. For a longer alarm use pack 1's stand_talking_angry. (5) look_back_and_sit carries needs: a chair. A scan of every clip's hand sockets (p2e/fix/armscan.py: a hand at least 20 px ahead of the head, at or above shoulder height) found one more case the round-1 sheets hid. In the LEFT profile, phone_conversation thrust the free right arm straight forward (forward-up in frame 4) and raised an open palm at head height (frames 12-18). Fixed by a motion edit: that arm is held at the Hand on Hip Gesture pose (0.5 s, his pass-1 idle clip) for the whole loop, so he phones with the left hand at his ear and the right arm down. arise got the same left-arm edit as the guard's. All of his edits are in p2e/fix/glb/regime_officer_p2e_fix.glb (spec p2e/fix/af_officer.json). Atlas: 23 clips, 2091 x 4661 px; pass-1 clips identical except round 1's knock_down fix; palette, alpha and window checks pass. Before / after: review/g8_p2e_fix_before_after_x2.png. Unreal: the arm edits exist only in the GLB copy in p2e/fix/glb/ (same rig, same clip names); the anim dir's FBX keeps Meshy's original arms - import the edited GLB for these clips, and never use the excluded gunshot_reaction with a profile camera.

judge.notes: 1) Cap lamp: the plan's lamp-ramp accent is absent (0 pixels of lamp #7a4a1a..#fff3c4 in miner_hauer.png and miner_hauer_c0.png). The clean-up or prototype matching removes it. Paint it from 3D: project the rig's 'headfront' node each frame. When it faces the camera (dot > 0), put 1 px lamp[3] '#ffd890' plus 1 px lamp[2] below it, outlined, and exempt the lamp class from the lone-pixel and island merge. Do the same for miner_hauer_c0. 2) ladder_climb_loop: render it seen from behind (camera behind the rig, as the hero's climb in judge_r2/hero_climb.png) on both sheets, keep inplaceY, and export 'dy' and 'lx' as the hero does. The clip rises 43.8 cm per 1.567 s loop = 23 px over 16 frames, so dy ≈ 1.44 px/frame; lx = midpoint of hand_l and hand_r minus ax. 3) Ground snap: idle -2/-3, drink -2/-3, ladder -6..+1, sneaky_walk +1..+3, walk 0..+2. 4) 'speed': sneaky_walk 93.8 cm / 2.833 s ≈ 17 px/s, cautious_crouch_walk_forward 151.2 / 1.133 ≈ 70 px/s; walk, run and injured_walk from foot slide. 5) Belt speckle (0.092, the group's highest): raise the island size for the metal and canvas classes on the belt ([4,8]) so battery and pouches read as two blocks. 6) Denim lit steps #323e5c / #4a5774 are off-palette until the owner adds RAMP.denim. If he declines, map them to steel[3] '#3d4446' and steel[4] '#4f5a5c'. 7) Skin deep step -> '#8d5245'.
judge.reroll: none: I3D c2 (white helmet with cap lamp, navy work clothes, tool belt, rubber boots) reads well and differs from every other figure. The c0 alternate (leather helmet, canvas) is the plan's period hauer but reads as a flat cap close to civilian_man; keep it as an alternate. The black strip from helmet to shoulder is the lamp cable. It can read as a ponytail but is acceptable.

clips.name: crouch_pull

clips.name: bend_over_pick_up
clips.note: 0.6-5.0 s of Male Bend Over Pick Up (the idle stand before / after is cut). Motion edit (p2f fix round): Meshy brought the object up to the chest with the elbow out, which on the left sheet stuck the near arm straight forward at shoulder / chin height (frames 15-34, the salute-risk shape); the right clavicle, arm and forearm are now slerped from 1.95 s (full from 2.5 s = frame 15) to a lowered hold - upper arm along the body, forearm forward, hand at belt height (p2e/fix/armfix.py + p2f/af_miner.json, targets from p2f/tools/target.py -> p2f/glb/miner_hauer_p2f_fix.glb; frames 0-10 and every other clip are the bought keys). handscan's 'up' hits in frames 6-8 are the bent-over back: the free left hand rests on the thigh, above the lowered head, not raised
clips.role: picks a small object off the floor with the right hand (frames 4-12), straightens and holds it in that hand at belt height in front of the belly, the elbow down (from frame 15; one-shot: hold the last frame; the hand_r socket = the object)

clips.name: catching_breath
clips.note: 3.8-7.0 s of Catching Breath: its jog in place (0-3.6 s, root motion) is cut
clips.role: exhausted after a run / the dust: bent over, hands on the knees, panting (no standing cough in the free library)

clips.name: headache_relief
clips.role: dizzy / wipes the brow: both hands to the head and temples (frames 0-19), then a tired wave-off at waist height

clips.name: sit_on_floor

clips.name: short_breathe_and_look_around
clips.role: looks around (alerted / searching), as the courier's and the guard's

clips.name: cower
clips.note: Stand Dodge 1 on the rig forward (as the cast's turns and reactions). A stand-in: it opens in a boxing guard (fists up at the face, frames 0-4) before the shielding turn

clips.note: a stand-in: the fists are a boxing guard, so it reads as backing off ready to fight rather than as fear
clips.role: backs away from a threat with the fists up at the chest (the nearest the free library has to hands-up: no surrender action; a raised open palm is the pass-1/2 salute rule); loop, moves backward (negative speed)

judge.notes: 1) Value separation: the tweed jacket (dust ramp) and trousers (burlap ramp) come out the same mid-dark olive-brown, so the figure reads as one flat mass (judge_r2/civ_b.png, civ_d.png). In cfg_civ.py MAN_M set 'trou' to st('basalt', 1, 2, 3, 4, 5); the 3D trousers are a cooler grey than the jacket. Alternatively, lift the jacket one step (st('dust', 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) and keep the trousers on burlap[0..3]. 2) Moustache: paint it from 3D (1-2 px of smog[7] at the projected 'headfront' node minus about 3 cm in y), since it is too small to class. 3) Skin deep step -> '#8d5245'. 4) Ground snap: idle -1..-3, chair_sit -4, stand_and_chat -1..-3, wave -3. 5) 'speed' for walk, run and push_and_walk_forward (foot slide).
judge.reroll: none: I3D c0 (flat cap, patched tweed jacket, dark waistcoat, baggy trousers) is the right old worker. The push loop (34 frames, standing start cut) and crouch_and_push one-shot read as shunting a tub.

assets.name: resistance_courier

judge.notes: (1) roll_behind_cover: frames 18-20 (right) and 16-18 (left) are headless; her head is bowed behind her shoulders while she turns. Start segment 2 after the turn, where the head shows again (about frame 21 right, 19 left), or re-render segment 2 turned so the head stays visible. Otherwise drop the clip from the web atlas (keep the FBX) and use crouch_look_around for hiding. (2) In the JSON, give the cover as an exact contact height rather than 'at most 0.69 m'. Her lowest body pixel is 27 px in frames 6 and 12, so the cover top should be about 27 px (0.5 m). (3) Optional: the wave turned +-0.8 rad is a 46-degree snap from the 0.35 profile idle; add turn-in and turn-out metadata or accept it. The concepts, I3D model, rig at 1.68 m, face ramp, belt row, walk, run, sneak, look-around, crouch, vault, ladder and collect clips are good and on the palette.

Sprites: 88 px (1.68 m at 52.5 px/m), 12 clips both facings, atlas 2430 x 2057 like the others (anims / left.anims, frames {x,y,w,h,ax,ay} + sockets): walk 8f loop; run 8f/12fps loop; idle 32f/6fps loop (0-5.3 s of Idle 3, loop end fitted); sneaky_walk 28f/10fps loop; short_breathe_and_look_around 47f/6fps; cautious_crouch_walk_forward 11f/10fps loop; crouch_look_around 35f/6fps loop; unarmed_vault 10f/12fps; ladder_climb_loop 16f/10fps loop (in place in y); wave_one_hand 33f/8fps (turned +-0.8 rad toward the viewer in the fix round); roll_behind_cover 34f/10fps (a dive over a cover of at most 0.69 m; two in-place segments 0-2.0 / 2.1-3.5 s: one straight line over the whole clip put the dive 1.2 m ahead of the anchor and out of the window); collect_object 36f/6fps. (1) The beard. The dark jaw in the right facing was not side hair. It was the skin ramp's deepest step, skinS #271713, on the shadowed jaw and on the pixels under the cap brim: the right camera sees her face turned away from the upper-left light, and the inner depth lines take that step too. Next to the brown-black jacket it read as a beard. Her face ramp is now skinM / skinM / skinL / skinL / skinL (#8d5245 / #b18465, all hero skin steps), so the jaw shading is mid-brown. x6 check against the judge's crop: review/g8_resistance_courier_face_x6.png (round 1 vs now, both facings). (2) The belt. The jacket's fabric belt (y 1.036-1.074 m, dark texels only) is painted leather-brown in a copy of the texture, chosen by each texel's bind-pose position (p2e/fix/texpaint.py). It now maps to the wood ramp: one row at the waist in both facings, and the rust scarf stays. The painted GLB copies (p2e/fix/glb/courier_*_fix.glb) are for the sprites only; the 3D kit GLB and the FBX files are unchanged. All 12 clips were re-rendered. (4) wave_one_hand is re-rendered turned toward the viewer: +0.8 rad on the right sheet, -0.8 on the left. assets.notes: Fix round, no credits. Size: the body floated 3 cm on remnants of the dropped feet, so its bottom is now clamped flat (objpatch clamp). It is re-imported at crate_a's size, 0.97 x 0.91 x 1.02 m. Front-left edge 49 px, top 56, ay 56, all equal to crate_a; size_m 1.28 x 1.09 against crate_a's 1.26 x 1.09. A one-row bump on the lid was trimmed so the tops match. Brackets are crate_a's steel corner L's on the front and side frames (steel[4] body, steel[5] lit, steel[3] shade; 214 steel px). The stray dark texture specks are wood again, so no coal or iron remains. The broken plank is a drawn 2 px wood[3] board with a wood[4] lit top edge. It sags 1 in 4 across the opening's upper left, ends in splinters and casts its shadow on the wall; the Meshy stub's dark hole was filled. Inside: the back planks are wood[2] with two wood[1] seams; the left inner wall and floor are a step darker (wood[1]), with receding wood[0] seams. Outline is OUTLINE, as the standable crates have. Kit: open front, feet removed, dequantized and welded (5.9k verts for 4.0k faces).
